notes: Read-Wilson graph atlas constructor (ALGO-CN-021). The hot path is two array indexes (POS table, then a tiny header read) plus a Graph::new + add_edges with at most 21 edges (K_7), so per-call cost is dominated by edge insertion — note rust_atlas_idx0 (zero edges) is 226 ns while idx1252 (21 edges) is 1.14 µs. The full 1253-graph walk lands at ~1.06 ms in release mode. python-igraph's Graph.Atlas pays a fixed ~85 µs/call (Cython entry path + Graph object construction) regardless of graph size, so the speedup is largest on the tiny graphs (376× on the null graph). Capture: `cargo bench --bench bench_atlas -- --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 3 --sample-size 30` on Darwin/M-series release; python baseline via `.venv/bin/python -m igraph` averaged over 500 iterations (20 for the walk). Medians (criterion middle column) reported for rust numbers.
